tool.name: graphql_specialist_check
tool.description:
Run the deterministic GraphQL-protocol-specific abuse tests against a single GraphQL endpoint.
Today GraphQL endpoints get a probabilistic subset of the actual API tested. This tool turns four GraphQL-specific abuse classes into a single deterministic call:
1. **Introspection probe** — issues the standard `__schema` query. When introspection is enabled, captures the type/field inventory and emits an info finding (CWE-200). The schema summary is returned in the result for downstream agent reasoning.
2. **Depth abuse** — sends a recursive depth query (`__schema` nested through `ofType`). When the server accepts a deeply-nested query without error, no max-depth is enforced (CWE-770, DoS via super-linear cost).
3. **Alias overloading** — sends N (default 100) aliased copies of `__schema` in a single request. When all N aliases come back in `data`, per-operation rate limiting is missing (CWE-770, DoS amplification + credential-stuffing rate-limit evasion).
4. **Batch query** — sends a JSON-array of N (default 50) operations. When the server processes all N as a list, batch support without per-op rate limiting is missing (CWE-770, same class as alias overloading).
Composes with cluster-A safety: every fetch routes through `proxy_manager.send_simple_request` when the proxy is available, so `--auth-cookie` / `--auth-bearer` / `--auth-basic` / `--header` / `--exclude-path` / `--rate-limit` apply automatically. Direct fallback uses the same env-driven `http_safety` middleware.
Pairs with `authz_matrix_check` — for field-level authorization across roles, pass the GraphQL endpoint URL into the matrix; for protocol-specific abuse, use this tool.
Use after recon (`bfs_crawl` + `fingerprint_tech_stack` confirms a GraphQL endpoint exists) or directly when the agent already knows the GraphQL URL.

parameter.name: depth_probe_max
parameter.description: Max nesting depth for the depth-abuse probe. Default 12. Most well-configured servers should reject > 5-7.

parameter.name: alias_count
parameter.description: Number of aliased operations sent in a single request to test alias-overloading. Default 100. Should be rejected by any well-configured server.

parameter.name: batch_size
parameter.description: Number of operations sent in a JSON-array batch. Default 50.

returns.description: {success, target_url, tests: {introspection, depth_abuse, alias_abuse, batch_abuse}}. Findings are emitted via the tracer (one info-severity for introspection-enabled, one high-severity for each accepted abuse class).
